big_idea: Bigger structures are MADE OF smaller 2D shapes and 3D objects.
learning_intention: We are learning to compose and decompose a structure into its parts.
student_learning_goal: I can compose and decompose a structure into its parts.
success_criteria: I can BUILD a structure from 3D parts.
I can NAME the parts I used.
I can DECOMPOSE a structure I see.
I can FIND 2D shapes inside 3D parts.
lesson_specific_materials: OPTIONAL: Trekker Tig and Compass Coco — if available; otherwise teacher voices both characters in two distinct voices, or substitutes two stuffed animals / paper-bag puppets / pictures on the anchor poster. Activity is unaffected.

minds_on.hook: Trekker Tig: Watch me COMPOSE a tower from 3 parts. Then DECOMPOSE — what's inside? Coco opens: 'BUILD it BIG, BREAK it small — both ways are MATH!'
minds_on.teacher_script:
Bring children to the carpet. Trekker Tig with backpack and 3 paper solid cards. 'Geometers — today we COMPOSE (build) and DECOMPOSE (break) structures.'

Define. 'COMPOSE = put together. DECOMPOSE = take apart.'

Demo. 'I'll BUILD a tower from 3 cards: cube on bottom, rectangular prism in middle, square pyramid on top.'

Stack them. 'My tower COMPOSES 3 parts: cube, prism, pyramid.'

Now flip. 'I'll DECOMPOSE this tower I see.' Show a structure card with a stacked cube + cylinder. 'I see: 1 cube and 1 cylinder.'

'Trekker Tig says — every STRUCTURE is made of named SOLIDS.'

Now zoom in. 'Each 3D solid is also made of 2D faces. The cube has 6 SQUARE faces. The pyramid has 1 SQUARE base + 4 TRIANGLE sides.'

'Trekker Tig says — 3D objects are MADE OF 2D shapes!'

Demo a second structure. 'A house: rectangular prism (body) + square pyramid (roof).'

Now each pair gets 4 Solid Cards. They COMPOSE 2 structures (e.g., 'tower of 3' and 'house of 2'). Then they get 4 Structure Cards to DECOMPOSE.

'Trekker Tig says — building and breaking are TWO sides of the same coin.'

steps.instruction: Hand out Solid Cards + Structure Cards. Pairs compose 4 structures.
Pairs decompose 4 structure cards: list the parts.
Stretch: identify 2D shapes inside one 3D part.
Help with naming — point at chart.

STRATEGY COMPARE 'Two ways to build it': Pairs compose the SAME target structure two different ways (e.g., 4-cube tower vs 4-cube L-shape both = 4 cubes). Class compares. Cite Battista (2007) spatial structuring.
steps.teacher_prompt: Coco: 'Same blocks, different shapes. The MATH counts BOTH as valid.'

differentiation.for_movement_learners: Build with real classroom objects. NO-MATERIALS VERSION: children compose structures using their own bodies and classroom objects (book stack = rectangular prism). Body becomes the construction set.

formative_check.what_to_look_for: Five signals: composes; decomposes; names parts; finds 2D inside 3D; consistency.

discussion_prompts: What 2D shape is in a CYLINDER?
consolidation.exit_routine: Coco's compose refrain — 'Coco says: BUILD it BIG, BREAK it small — both ways are MATH!' (3x). Each child shows one structure decomposed into its parts.

expanded_walkthrough.title: When the child names ONE part of a multi-part structure — repairing the partial-decompose trap at Grade 3
expanded_walkthrough.rationale:
On compose/decompose, the Grade-3 trap is partial-decompose: child decomposes top-half but leaves bottom intact. Battista (2007) on spatial structuring + Sarama & Clements (2009) on composition trajectories frame this.

Yesterday Tig sorted solids. Today we BUILD and BREAK with them. Lesson 3 congruent faces; Lesson 4 map+move; Lesson 5 capstones.
expanded_walkthrough.setup: Decompose activity. Child sees a tower (cube + prism + pyramid) and writes only 'cube'.
expanded_walkthrough.teacher_script:
Crouch. 'Trekker Tig asks — what's ABOVE the cube? What's on TOP?'

Guide. 'Look at the WHOLE structure. Bottom to top. What do you see?'

Generalise. 'Trekker Tig says — DECOMPOSE means name EVERY part, not just the easy one.'

If still partial: trace the structure with finger. 'Here's part 1, part 2, part 3 — name each.'
common_misconceptions: Only big parts count. (Repair: small parts too.)
recovery_moves: DIAGNOSTIC A — child partial-decomposes: drill 'EVERY part comes apart'; physical demo with full disassembly.
DIAGNOSTIC B — child decomposes correctly but cannot recompose: force 'put them back EXACTLY as found' as a check.
DIAGNOSTIC C — child can do both but cannot articulate: force the sentence frame 'I broke ___ into ___ pieces.'

parts_outline.task: Compose 2 structures: draw or write the parts used.
